Monday, December 5, 2022  7:00 PM  Council Chambers/Teleconference

In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, 2521, 2530, and 2534, due to the continuing state of emergency, including
masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being
broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate virtually in the meeting in the following
ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 9128) from any phone, Meeting ID:
865 4580 5838 Passcode: 924437. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the carolc@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m.
prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Planning Commission for their consideration and included
as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 865 4580 5838 Passcode: 924437.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are available on
the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, DECEMBER 5, 2022

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:05 p.m. in person and via teleconference pursuant to
Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low*, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  Carman

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

* Commissioner Low joined the meeting at 7:07 p.m. by phone due to technical issues.

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER 7, 2022

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 7,
  2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220479; 5 PLEASANT HILL DRIVE, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: MAURICIO ARREGOCES AND FRANCESBEL
  ARREGOCES; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220480)
  for a 2,909 square foot single-story addition and 902 square-foot second-story addition to
  an existing single story single-family residence. The proposal requires a Minor Deviation
  (MD-220483) for a reduction of the required front yard area by no more than ten percent
  (10%), from 4,709 square feet to 4,581 square feet. A second Minor Deviation (MD-
  220495) is required for an encroachment into the front yard that does not project closer
  than the forwardmost building line, for the purposes of a new front porch and one-car
  garage.

Associate Planner Flores presented Planning Application No. PA-220479 summarizing the staff
report. He noted that there was an error in the staff report; the addition for the first floor is for 134
sq. ft.; the total for the first floor, including the addition, will be 2,909 sq. ft.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 5, 2022
  1
 Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-220479, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for first and second story
additions to a single-story single-family residence, including a change of the architectural style
from Ranch to Mediterranean; and Minor Deviations (MD-220483 and MD-220495) for a reduction
of the front yard by no more than ten percent and an encroachment into the front yard no closer
than the forwardmost building line, subject to the conditions of approval.

Keith Johnson, Architect welcomed questions. The Planning Commissioners had no questions or
comments for Mr. Johnson.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 220479 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OF
  APPROVAL.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that there is a 20-day appeal period whereby any member of the public
or the City Council by its own motion may appeal this decision.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 220424; ADDRESS: 2 DOBBIN LANE, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CA 90274; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
  220425) for a 491 square-foot single-story addition and a 776 square-foot second-story
  addition to an existing two-story single-family residence. The proposal requires a Variance
  (V-220485) for a portion of the existing second story that contains an existing
  nonconforming height-to-setback ratio on the south side of the home. The proposal also
  requires a Minor Deviation (MD-220426) for a reduction of the required front yard area by
  no more than ten percent (10%), from 3,318 square feet to 3,309 square feet.

Associate Planner Flores presented Planning Application No. 220424 summarizing the staff
report.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff received one correspondence from a neighbor, which
was provided to the Planning Commission prior to the meeting. The correspondence was an
inquiry on whom to contact regarding issues during construction.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, Open the
Public Hearing; Take public testimony; Discuss the issues; Close the Public Hearing; and Adopt
Resolution No. PA-220424, approving the project, and in accordance with the California
Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code § 21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), the application has
been determined to be Categorically Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing
Facilities.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about a change to the roof line. Associate Planner stated
that it will be a straight roof line.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked if this change would require re-noticing of the project. Director Naughton
stated that the change is minor and does not require re-noticing.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSINER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

Reiko Michlig, Project Designer, stated that this lot is smaller than the standard sized lot in this
zoning district, and explained the challenges with this property.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked about the nonconforming portion of the home and if it was part of the
original construction. Director Naughton stated that as far as staff can tell, this was part of the
original construction.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if, due to the concerns of the neighbor at 6 Dobbin Lane
regarding construction issues, can the contractor be required to acknowledge that there are

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 5, 2022
  2
 parking issues and must adhere to construction hours. Ms. Michlig stated that she believes that
this addressed when obtaining building permits and stated that these issues will also be
addressed upon hiring a contractor.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked for further questions or comments from those present and on Zoom;
there were no further questions or comments.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  Adopt Resolution No. PA-220424.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated the Planning Commission has adopted Resolution No. PA-220424,
approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220425), a Variance (V-220485),
and a Minor Deviation (MD-220426). There is a 20-day appeal period whereby any member of
the public or the City Council by its own motion may appeal this decision.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the resurfacing project in the commercial district.
Director Naughton stated that it is her understanding that the project is being postponed until after
the Holidays.

CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about the sale of the Promenade and about the Norris Theatre
lawsuit. Director Naughton stated that she believes there has been resolution to the parking issue
and did not go to trial. In regard to the new ownership of the Promenade, their plan is to attract
new businesses, including more restaurants and activities-based uses.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the new owners have reached out to him, and they
have great plans for this project.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton stated that there have been new bills passed regarding ADUs and JADUs that
go into effect at the beginning of 2023. Staff will not be bringing the ordinance to the Planning
Commission, but instead an urgency ordinance will be going forward to the City Council at its
meeting in late January. The changes are relatively minor.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked if ADUs would be allowed in front yards. Director Naughton stated that
if there is no other place to build an ADU, then it would be allowed in the front yard. Most lots in
the city would not preclude construction anywhere else on properties. Horse keeping areas also
cannot preclude construction of an ADU.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – NOVEMBER 8, 2022

CHAIR SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting to February 6, 2023 at 7:35 p.m.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 5, 2022
  3
 Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Schachter, Chair
